structure: A corpus of 50 Playwright trace zips (one per test, folder name = test id) from the INS frontend's fit specs at INS frontend 406e300, all passed, with report.json (npm output precedes the JSON; the JSON starts at the first line beginning with '{') mapping each test to its folder. All 50 are in scope (scope is every <test>/trace.zip); I selected by listing every folder that holds a trace.zip, no substring filtering. Split by spec file: smoke.fit.spec.js (1 core journey: sign in, dashboard, add, view, delete an address), features/address-book/fit add (19: render, axe, 7 required-field errors, 8 over-length errors, malformed email, error-state axe, save, cancel), delete (4), edit (7), list (6), view (5), and features/dashboard (6, AC1-AC5 plus axe). Pages found, in journey order: (1) Dashboard at / with search by notification reference, sort select, a table (Reference number, Status, Origin country, Commodity, Arrival date, Action) and a 'No notifications found' empty state; (2) Address book list at /address-book (search, Add a new address, table Name/Address/Country/Action, pagination at 25 per page, empty state 'You have no addresses yet.', success banner after add/edit/delete); (3) Add address details at /address-book/add (form, always reachable from list; error summary state on invalid POST); (4) Address details at /address-book/<id> (summary list, Edit and Delete buttons, Back link); (5) Edit address details at /address-book/<id>/edit; (6) Delete address confirmation at /address-book/<id>/delete. Conditional: success banner (only after a successful add, edit or delete, shown above the H1), pagination (only above 25 addresses), empty state, error summary and per-field errors (only after an invalid submit). Dashboard 'View' links leave the INS frontend for the animals frontend on localhost:3000 (/live-animals/notifications/<ref> or .../notification-view); those pages are out of this source. Tooling decision: `tim distil trace ... -- open` failed with TraceVersionError (the traces were written by a newer Playwright than tim's viewer supports), so no playwright subcommand was usable. I unzipped each trace into the working folder and read the raw trace files directly: the action list from before events in 1-trace.trace, rendered DOM from the frame-snapshot events (full-page snapshots at each navigation, rendered main content with jq), the network log from 1-trace.network, and the spec source embedded in each zip under src/. Refs therefore use the form `<test folder> call@<n>` where n is the Playwright callId of the action whose full-page snapshot was read, or `<test folder> src` for the spec source embedded in the zip. Validation messages for the fields I did not snapshot are taken from the embedded spec source, which asserts the rendered text and passed in every trace, so they are verbatim rendered copy; the empty-name and over-255-name error states were read from the rendered DOM directly. Platform chrome (service header, phase banner, footer) is skipped except where it is the service navigation, which the INS frontend owns. Seed data in the traces is the stub address book (Stub Farm 1..30 in the pagination test), stub org ids and a fixed three-notification dashboard dataset. Credential-shaped values: the CSRF crumb hidden input values are not copied.

claims.statement: All INS frontend pages in the traces are built entirely from GOV.UK Design System components (summary list, table, pagination, notification banner, error summary, buttons, service navigation, phase banner, inputs and select) with no non-govuk component classes other than govuk-!-spacing and width utilities; the only custom class seen is on the header ('app-header').

claims.statement: The address book and dashboard are rendered server-side by the INS frontend over plain GET and POST requests: add and delete are POSTs that answer 302 to the list; no client-side data calls (XHR/fetch) appear in the network log.

claims.statement: The traces do not show the calls the INS frontend server makes to its backends (the address book system of record, the ins-backend notification read model) or what they return, so the data source for the dashboard and address list, and the call shapes, are not recorded.
claims.note: The fit run uses stubbed data; only the browser's requests are in the network log.
